chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us, he said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: al-Abbas ibn Amir narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Rizq, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: "O Ishaq, how do you dispose of the zakat of your wealth when it becomes due?" I said: "People come to my house and I give them."

Then he said to me: "I see that you, O Ishaq, have only humiliated the believer. Beware, beware! For indeed Allah the Exalted says: Whoever humiliates a righteous servant of Mine has indeed prepared himself to confront Me in war."

key_terms.أذللت: Humiliated: from the root dh-l-l, to make lowly
key_terms.المؤمن: The believer: person of faith whose dignity is sacred
key_terms.زكاة: Zakat: obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about humiliating the poor when giving zakat?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) admonished his companion Ishaq ibn Ammar for distributing zakat by making recipients come to his house, explaining that this humiliates the believers. The Imam reinforced the gravity by quoting a divine saying (hadith qudsi) in which God warns that whoever humiliates His righteous servants has declared war against Him. This teaching emphasizes that charity must preserve the dignity of the poor.
